answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity capital lock, not on counting accounts. Each identity posts a slashable bond staked for the epoch, and reward share is paid by stake weight, never by headcount. The bond is the anchor of admission: to win influence an attacker must lock real, idle capital, and splitting one funded wallet into a thousand look-alike keys still yields one stake's weight. The beacon of a live seat is that escrowed collateral, so every extra identity pays the same entry cost, and an oasis of fakes earns nothing. Buying influence scales linearly with sunk, slashable cost.
